name: workflow
description: Backlog-driven work loop as two skills. /backlog writes one backlog item and gets its acceptance criteria approved; with --survey it researches the repository and the outside with parallel agents, has a separate judge agent filter the candidates, and shows them with draft acceptance criteria. /start takes one item from plan to merge in one run: baseline, stack checks, implementation, deslop, verification, acceptance criteria checked only with outside evidence or a separate judge, review with code-review plus the stack reviewers of enabled plugins, valid findings fixed without asking, then one final message for the decisions only the user can make and the merge. Claude invokes both on its own when you ask to add or start a backlog item. It asks only about irreversible or outward actions, shared config changes, product or taste decisions, choosing what to do, and states that could lose work; everything else is decided and logged in the item file with the reason and the cost of being wrong. There is no plan approval. Both skills open a sub-session by default (start in its own worktree on a w/ branch); --here, or no session tool, runs in the current session. The start skill carries a when-to-what index over 24 principles, 14 skills (architect, blast-radius, how, why, a project verification skill with a feature map, control-ui, control-cli, deslop, verify-this and more) and 5 playbooks (bug-fix, refactoring, prototype, perf-issue, hillclimb) adapted from pstack and cursor-team-kit, read when they apply. Sub-sessions opened from a Fable session run on the latest model one step lower at high effort. Fix-and-recheck loops stop and hand over after three failed fixes of the same criterion. A Stop hook re-runs the base branch's verify command when an item is marked done (and says so if the branch changed it), also after another Stop hook such as /goal has blocked. Web and server ports are split per item. Mechanical steps run as tested scripts: picking a free item port, and running the branch's new tests against the base branch's source to flag tests that do not prove the fix.
